column1: # Exit criterion E2 — exact-title top-1 must be 100%.
# "Typing a film's name and not getting that film first" is the failure a search engine
# is not allowed to have. E2 sets the bar at 100%, not "high", which is why the
# implementation short-circuits ranking entirely for an exact match rather than trusting
# EVERY EXPECTED ID IS WRITTEN FROM INDEPENDENT KNOWLEDGE of what the film is, not by
# running the search and recording its answer. A fixture generated from the code it
# tests cannot fail. The E5 anime fixture was wrong four times on its first run and the
# matcher was wrong none — so a disagreement here is worth investigating in both
# directions before assuming the code is at fault.
# The queries are deliberately awkward. A corpus of clean titles would pass on the day
# it was written and catch nothing afterwards.
# HONESTLY: the first run scored 38/44, and FOUR of the six failures were this file
# being wrong rather than the code. Where several works share an exact title, search
# returns the most popular one — and I had asserted the version I think of as canonical:
#   and then there were none   code: 2015 (49,811 votes)   I said: 1945 (18,802)
#   hunter x hunter            code: 2011 (204,023)        I said: 1999 (12,528)
#   fullmetal alchemist        code: Brotherhood (257,061) I said: 2003 (87,114)
# The code is right. For a ranking, the most popular work bearing the exact title is
# what someone typing it most likely means, and E2's intent is "you get a film with that
# title", not "you get the one I would have picked". Corrected below, with the reasoning
# kept so the next person does not quietly re-assert my preferences.
# A fifth failure — "Am*lie" — was a query I invented to test an FTS5 wildcard. Nobody
# types an asterisk expecting Amélie, and a fixture entry that tests nothing real is
# The sixth was a genuine bug: `normalise` folded punctuation but not diacritics, while
# the FTS5 index folded both. The two halves of the same search disagreed about what a
# title is, so "Nausicaa" missed "Nausicaä". Both now fold via NFD.
